answer: Private defence is a legal right that permits an individual to protect themselves from an assault that poses a reasonable threat of death. For example, if a person (A) is attacked by a mob intending to kill him, and the only way for A to defend himself is to fire at the mob, he may do so even if it risks harming innocent children present. In this scenario, A would not be committing an offence if any children are harmed as a result of his actions, as he was acting in self-defence against a life-threatening situation. This principle is outlined in Section 44 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which states that the right of private defence extends to situations where there is a risk to innocent persons (chunk__node__BNS_S44_BODY, Section 44 Body, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023).
summary_answer: Private defence allows a person to protect themselves from an imminent threat, even if it risks harming innocent bystanders.
